1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Panov Attack, Modern Defence

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.strategy: Develops the bishop against the knight that guards d5. If the knight is exchanged, Black either gets doubled pawns or loses a key defender of d5, so Black has to meet the threat with care. White plays for a sharp, open game.
A calm developing move that adds a defender to d4, which the knight on c6 presses, and prepares castling. White keeps all options open and lets Black decide between a sharp and a solid set-up.

Gives d5 a third defender and releases the dark-squared bishop. The cost is a passive light-squared bishop on c8. Black aims for a solid set-up in which the d5 pawn is safe and White's initiative has to be earned.

Pins the knight against the queen and adds pressure on d4, because the knight on f3 is its defender. The sharpest reply: Black plays for tactics based on the pinned knight and for damage to White's pawn structure.
1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Panov Attack, Modern Defence, Mieses Line

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.strategy: The solid answer: it adds a defender to d5 and opens the f8-bishop, and the pin on f6 is harmless, since Black can retake there with the queen or the g-pawn. Black keeps a sound centre and develops without concessions.
1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Panov Attack, Modern Defence, Carlsbad Line

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.strategy: Pins the knight on c3 against the king, so it cannot take on d5, and hits the centre from the side. The queen is exposed on a5, though, so Black must keep the initiative: White can unpin and carry on with the development.
1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Panov Attack, Modern Defence, Czerniak Line

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.strategy: Attacks d4 for a second time and the undefended b2 pawn, so White has to react at once instead of developing. Black invites sharp play with the queen out early; the double pressure brings counterplay, but the knight on f6 stays under the bishop's fire.
1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Panov Attack, Modern Defence, Reifir-Spielmann Line

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 Nc6 5.N.strategy: Takes the pawn at once, but it cannot be kept: the bishop retakes it, and Black has given up the central tension for little. White then stands freer, with quicker development and the pin on f6 still in place.
